description: Implications of Digital Infrastructure Growth for Public Water Consumption: A Time-Lagged Analysis of Data Center Expansion in the Water-Stressed Southwestern United States is a data set deposited in psu.datacom by its authors S. Rastegar, B. Gaertner (Pennsylvania State University). The rapid expansion of large-scale data centers (DCs) in the chronically water-stressed Southwestern United States presents a significant challenge to regional water management, a problem compounded by a critical knowledge gap stemming from the lack of site-specific water consumption data. Coverage: national (US); the metadata date the deposit to 2026. The formats are not stated in the metadata. It is reached through its DOI or landing page, listed on this page. Access is free of charge and open according to the repository. The licence is not stated (no licence in the DataCite metadata read on 2026-09-29). Caveats: written from the DataCite metadata (title, abstract, subjects and rights) read on 2026-09-29; the deposit itself was not opened or downloaded, so its contents, quality and current availability were not checked. It can support multi-sector infrastructure risk and planning studies. Related records: none catalogued yet for this repository.
